**Article Details for PMID: 42933389**

**Title:** In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial.

**Authors:** Guoling Li, Feng Han, Cuijin Wang, Ming Jin, Jiajia Lin, Hainan Zhang, Xiudong Yan, Xing Wang, Xinyan Sun, Yiqun Yuan, Siyuan Zhang, Shuaishuai Zhang, Jingyan Zhu, Yichao Xu, Yingyan Wang, Yujiao Deng, Fangxin Li, Linyu Shi, Alvin Luk, Ning Wang, Hui Yang, Jiwen Wang

**Journal:** Cell
**Publication Date:** 2026-10-26
**DOI:** 10.1016/j.cell.2026.09.059

**Abstract:**
We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.
